D011-D016_h001.question: Lately, I’ve just been feeling so wound up all the time—like I can’t settle into the moment, even during my own yoga classes. It’s not one thing in particular; my mind jumps from work stuff, like whether my students are really benefiting, to wondering if I’ll make enough from private sessions next month, then suddenly I’m thinking about my mom’s health, or what if I get injured and can’t teach anymore. It just spirals. I notice my shoulders are always tight, and my back aches constantly, like I’m carrying this weight even when I’m lying in Savasana. My arms and legs feel heavy after even a gentle session, and I’m not sure why—there’s no injury, but everything’s so stiff. I try to breathe through it, but the tension doesn’t ease. It’s been like this for a while—months, maybe? I wouldn’t say I’m obsessed with the thoughts, and I don’t think I’m catastrophizing any more than anyone else might, but it’s persistent. I don’t know if it’s stress or something more, but it’s starting to get in the way of showing up as I want to—for my students, and for myself.
D011-D016_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D011-D016_h001.answer: A & D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling this constant weight, like I can’t catch my breath even when nothing’s wrong. It’s been going on for a while now—months, maybe? Work’s been the same, nothing out of the ordinary, but I can’t seem to settle my mind. My body’s always tight, like I’m braced for a fall or waiting for something bad to happen. My shoulders, my back—everything’s stiff, even when I’m off the clock. And my jaw… I’ve caught myself clenching it so hard, especially at night. Woke up with headaches a few times. My wife says she hears me grinding my teeth.

I keep trying to calm down, tell myself it’s nothing, focus on the job or the game on TV, but the thoughts just come back. Not really thoughts, though—more like a hum in the back of my head. “What if this goes wrong?” “What if I missed something?” I don’t obsess over it, but I can’t just let it go either. I’m not doing anything different to fix it, no routines or checking, just… stuck. I want to relax, but I feel like I’m wired wrong. Doesn’t matter how tired I am—I stay wound up.
D011-D016_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D011-D016_h002.answer: A & D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h003.question:
I’ve been feeling constantly on edge for months—like I’m stuck in turbulence that never ends. As a flight attendant, I’m used to being busy and alert, but this is different. My mind just won’t shut off, even when I’m off duty. I try to relax, especially since I’m married and we’ve been wanting to start a family, but I can’t seem to calm down. I worry about everything and nothing all at once—things at work, my health, little misunderstandings with people—and it just loops. I’ve tried distracting myself, taking warm baths, even journaling, but the thoughts come right back. 

Physically, I feel like I’m wound too tight—like a spring ready to snap. My shoulders and the back of my neck are always so tense, like knots I can’t massage away. I’ve had headaches pretty regularly now, and I catch myself pacing in the crew lounge or clenching my jaw without realizing it. 

I don’t know if it’s stress or something more, but it’s starting to affect my sleep and how present I can be, even at home. It’s been going on for more than half a year, maybe longer. I just feel… on. All the time.
D011-D016_h003.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D011-D016_h003.answer: A & D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h004.question: I’ve been feeling… off… for the past few months—maybe longer. Ever since Margaret passed, it’s like I can’t settle. Out in the woods, I used to find peace, but now even the quiet feels heavy, like something’s coming. I keep asking myself, “What if the trail floods?” or “What if a hiker goes missing?” Not because there’s any sign of it—just that I can’t shake the feeling that I should be preparing, watching, doing *something*. I try to push the thoughts away, take a long walk, fix the radio, but they come back just the same. My body’s always tight—shoulders up near my ears, jaw clenched. Feels like I’m standing at attention even when I’m sitting. The other rangers joke that I’m wound tighter than a watch spring, and they’re not wrong. I just can’t seem to turn it off, even when there’s nothing to fix. It’s not like I’m seeing visions or having strange urges—nothing like that. And I don’t think I worry more than any man should about storms or injuries out here. But still… I can’t relax the way I used to. Not since she’s been gone.
D011-D016_h004.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D011-D016_h004.answer: A & D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—nothing I can really put my finger on, but it’s like my mind won’t shut off. I’ll be on the train, running the line, and suddenly I’ll get stuck on these “what if” thoughts—like, *What if the signal changes and I miss it? What if I mishear a dispatch?* They’re not full-on images or urges, just… questions that loop. It’s not like I think I’ll actually do anything wrong, but I can’t let it go.  

I feel tense all the time, like I’m wound too tight. My jaw’s been bothering me—clenching, I guess, especially during shifts—and I’ve had headaches from it. Sitting still? Almost impossible. I pace between runs, even when I should be resting.  

I don’t know if it’s overthinking or just stress, but it’s hard to focus. I’ll be doing my job fine, then a random worry pops in and throws me off. I don’t check things more than usual or do any rituals or anything—just mental spinning.  

It’s not every second, and some days are okay, but enough that I notice. I don’t know if this is normal pressure or something more. I just want it to stop running in circles.
D011-D016_h005.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D011-D016_h005.answer: A & D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h006.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a while now—maybe the past few months, maybe a bit longer. I can’t quite pinpoint when it started, but there’s this constant hum in the back of my mind, like something’s off even when everything’s okay. I worry, sure, but not about anything specific—more like a general sense that I’m waiting for something to go wrong, though I can’t say what. It’s not like I’m obsessing over germs or counting things or anything like that; it just feels like my brain doesn’t shut down, even when I’m not actively stressed.

At night, I sleep a lot—too much, maybe. My husband’s mentioned it. I’ll go to bed early, sleep nine, ten hours, sometimes nap after work, but I still wake up feeling heavy, like I haven’t rested at all. It’s not insomnia—I can fall asleep easily—but I feel drowsy even after full nights. During the day, though, I feel jumpy. My muscles are tight, I can’t sit still during my lunch break, and I’ve caught myself pacing in the pharmacy stockroom for no reason. I’ve checked prescription logs twice sometimes, not because I think I made a mistake necessarily—more just to quiet the restlessness. But I wouldn’t say I’m trapped in any cycle of thoughts or rituals. Just… wound up, all the time.
D011-D016_h006.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D016_h006.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h007.question:
I’ve been feeling… off for months now—probably half a year or more. Most days, my mind just won’t shut off. Not that I can point to one thing, really—just a constant hum of unease, like something’s always about to go wrong. It’s not any one worry, more like the feeling itself sticks around, no matter what I’m doing.  

Driving the taxi—twelve, sometimes fourteen hours a day—it used to help clear my head. Now, my body feels tight the whole time, like I’m gripping the wheel even when I’m not. My shoulders, neck, back—they’re always stiff, even when I try to relax. I don’t remember the last time I felt loose, at ease.  

And sleep? I’m up most nights by 4:30, sometimes earlier. Once I’m awake, I can’t get back. I lie there, wired, heart not racing exactly, but just… on. Not panicked, just *there*. I don’t have these bad thoughts or images—I’m not checking things or doing rituals or anything like that. It’s just this low, constant pressure, like I’ve got a radio stuck between stations and can’t tune it in. I can’t tell if it’s my mind or my body bothering me more.
D011-D016_h007.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D016_h007.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for a while now—months, really. It’s like my mind won’t shut off. I worry about work, sure, picking up rides, fares adding up, or breaking down on the highway. But then it slips into other things—my kid not calling back, bills piling up, even weird stuff like whether I left the garage open back at my old house, even though I don’t live there anymore. It’s not like I’m double-checking things over and over or anything, it’s just… always there.  

Sleep’s been rough. I’ll get in bed exhausted, but my body feels like it’s locked up, shoulders tight, jaw clenched. Then I have these dreams—once I was stuck in traffic and the cars around me started sinking into the road, like the pavement was swallowing them. Woke up sweating, heart slamming. I’ve had a few like that—nothing consistent, just… bad.  

I don’t know if it’s stress or just getting older. I used to shrug things off, but now everything feels heavier. I’m not snapping at people or avoiding routes or doing rituals—I just can’t seem to relax. Even when I’m sitting still, I feel like I’m bracing for something.
D011-D016_h008.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D016_h008.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h009.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for a while now—about six months, maybe longer. Every morning, I wake up around 4 a.m., wide awake, heart kind of racing, and no matter how hard I try, I can’t drift back. It’s like my mind just… starts running. I lie there stiff, my shoulders tight, jaw clenched, like my body forgot how to relax. 

I tutor kids from home, so my days are pretty quiet, just me and my schedule. But lately, even small things—a student canceling, a missed email—set off this heaviness in my chest. I keep replaying conversations, wondering if I said the right thing, if they’ll come back, if I’ll lose more students. I don’t know—it’s not that I think disasters will happen, but the not knowing? That’s what gets to me. What if things just… fall apart?

I don’t have rituals or anything, no checking or repeating words in my head. But sometimes thoughts stick—like a note left hanging—and I can’t seem to drop them. I’m not sure if it’s overthinking or something else. I just feel trapped in the “what if,” like I’m bracing for something, but I don’t even know what.
D011-D016_h009.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D016_h009.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h010.question:
I’ve just turned 57, and honestly, I don’t know when I last felt truly calm. As a principal, there’s always something—staff meetings, parent concerns, district evaluations—and I keep thinking if I miss one detail, the whole school could fall apart. Like last week, a teacher submitted a form a day late, and I couldn’t stop thinking the state would audit us, we’d lose funding, kids would suffer. It sounds extreme, I know, but in the moment, it feels real.  

Most nights, I sleep ten, even twelve hours, but I wake up exhausted, like I’ve been running in my dreams. My husband says I look drained. And even when I’m sitting at my desk, I can’t stay still—legs shaking, fingers tapping. It’s like I’m wound too tight, like a spring about to snap.  

I try to push through it—school needs me—but it’s wearing me down. I don’t know if this is just stress, or if something’s really off. I’m not having strange thoughts or doing rituals, but the worry… it just loops. Not constant, but when it hits, it’s like a wave I can’t swim out of. I can’t tell if it’s normal pressure or something more.
D011-D016_h010.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D011-D016_h010.answer: D & C. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h011.question: I’ve been feeling off for about six months now. I sleep a lot—like, I’ll go to bed early and still wake up feeling wiped, and sometimes I nap during lunch even if I don’t mean to. But no matter how much I rest, I’m always exhausted. At work, it’s hard to keep up. I love the animals, but the stress of the clinic, the pace… my mind just races. Thoughts jump in out of nowhere—like, I’ll be drawing blood from a dog and suddenly think, *What if I made a mistake on the last one?* Even though I know I didn’t. It’s not that I’m afraid something bad will happen tomorrow or next week, just that these worries pop up and won’t leave. They’re just… there. And I can’t focus sometimes. I used to manage fine, but since the divorce, it’s like my brain doesn’t shut off—even when I’m sleeping too much. I don’t check things or repeat actions or anything like that. It’s more like my mind gets stuck on random things at the worst times. I don’t know if it’s anxiety or just burnout, but it’s making everything harder.
D011-D016_h011.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D011-D016_h011.answer: A & B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h012.question: I’ve been sleeping a lot lately—like, way more than I used to. I’ll go to bed at ten and wake up at noon, sometimes even later. I thought more rest would help me feel better, but honestly, I’m more drained. It’s like my brain just… stops working after an hour or two of thinking. I’m in pre-production for a new film, and I used to thrive on this part—the planning, the vision—but now I can’t stay focused long enough to get through a script. It’s frustrating because I *know* I should be able to pull myself together, but when I try to shut off the thoughts, they just come back louder. I’ll distract myself with work or music, even just walking around the house, but it doesn’t matter. Whatever’s bothering me just follows me around. I can’t point to one thing—it’s not like I’m obsessing over locks or anything specific. It’s more like a constant hum, something vague I can’t name. I’ve been like this for a few months now. D011-D016_h013.question:
I’m a surgery resident, so my schedule’s pretty intense—long hours, high stakes. Lately, I’ve just been feeling… off. I sleep five to six hours a night, sometimes more if I’m lucky, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all. It’s like my body’s tired no matter what. That constant fatigue makes it harder to keep up during the day, especially during long cases or overnight calls.

My mind’s always running—little things at work, a procedure I assisted with, a patient’s lab value—suddenly pop into my head in the middle of doing something else. I don’t dwell on them, and I don’t feel like I have to do anything about them, but they’re just… there. Like background noise I can’t turn down. I keep thinking, “Did I miss something?” or “What if that patient decompensates?” It doesn’t spiral, but it’s enough to pull my attention away during rounds or even when I’m trying to eat.

I wouldn’t say I’m overwhelmed, and I’m not checking things over and over or stuck in rituals. But the mental static? It never really stops. It’s been like this for a few months now.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D011-D016_h014.question:

I work at the zoo, and I love being around the animals, especially the primates; they’re predictable in a way people aren’t. But lately, even during feeding rounds or cleaning enclosures, my mind just… floods. Random thoughts pop up—like, “What if I left the gate unlocked?” or “Did I wash my hands properly after handling the food?” It’s not like I *think* anything bad will happen, exactly—it just *nags* at me, and I can’t focus.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D011-D016_h015.question:
I’ve been waking up around 4 or 5 most mornings, even when I’m exhausted. My mind’s already racing—thinking about things I need to do at the shop, whether I remembered to order enough lilies, if the arrangements for Saturday’s wedding will hold up. It’s not that I *want* to be up then, but I can’t seem to shut it off. Once I’m awake, I just lie there, and eventually, I give up and head into the greenhouse early.  

Most days, I feel drained before I even start. It used to energize me, arranging flowers, making something beautiful, but now it takes so much just to get through the motions. My husband’s been patient, but I can tell he notices I’ve been quiet, withdrawn.  

The weird part is, thoughts just pop into my head—like, “What if I forget to deliver an arrangement?” or “What if I left the gas on?”—and I can’t shake them right away. I don’t do anything special about them—no checking or rituals—but they stick around and make it hard to focus when I’m tying bouquets or helping a customer. It’s not constant, but it’s frequent enough to be frustrating. I just can’t seem to get back to feeling like myself.

A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D011-D016_h016.question:

At work, I keep going over whether I balanced the drawer right, even though I’ve done it a thousand times. Then I’ll start thinking about my son’s school project, or the mortgage, or if my husband’s okay after his long drives. D011-D016_h017.question:

D011-D016_h019.question:

I worry about my writing deadlines, then suddenly I’m thinking about my wife’s health, then our finances, then whether I locked the door. It jumps around. D011-D016_h020.question:

I don’t know what I’d do if anything changed—what if business slows, or the rent goes up, or one of my girls calls in sick? It’s not just work, though. I worry about my daughter’s job, my grandson’s schooling, even little things like whether I turned off the oven, though I *know* I check it.

Even getting out of bed some mornings feels heavy, like I’m moving through syrup.  

I try to focus, really I do, but the worries just drift in—quietly, not shouting, just… there. I wouldn’t say I’m overwhelmed, exactly. A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D011-D016_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling kind of... stuck in my head lately. Like, things start small—maybe I’ll think about an upcoming wedding I’m shooting, and whether the lighting will be right, or if the couple will be difficult. But then that turns into wondering if I’m falling behind on editing, even though I know I’m not. And then suddenly I’m thinking about money, or whether we should have kids, or if my husband’s annoyed with me for working so much. It keeps spiraling.
